card.title: Photo sync: should new photos keep syncing while the laptop is offline? (uses a little more phone storage)
card.body:
Your phone already keeps a short list of photos waiting to sync. Today it waits for the laptop before sending anything, so a long trip means nothing moves until you're home. Keeping a local queue means sync resumes on its own.

Why now: The first version is being built now; this decides its scope.

- Local queue (proposal): keeps up to 500 photos, sends the oldest first, and pauses when the phone is low on space.
- Cost: up to about 2 GB of extra phone storage while you're away.
- Either way it gets a review before shipping; nothing changes on your laptop until you say yes.
- Related edge case: a brand-new phone (no queue yet) waits for the laptop the first time.

If you do not answer: We build the simple version: sync waits for the laptop.

[Design (one page)](https://example.com/design/photo-sync)

choices.label: Yes: keep a local queue, ~2 GB max (Recommended)

replies.text: Yes. Nothing depends on it before Monday; I'll keep it open until then.

The trial works with a sample album. Moving your old albums means copying them to the chosen drive; your current library stays where it is.

Why now: You asked to see this; it's the last step before real use.

- The move happens only after the review; this card only picks where.
- The originals stay until you clear them, so moving is reversible.

If you do not answer: Nothing moves; your albums stay where they are.
